title: L5 spondylolysis/spondylolisthesis: a comprehensive review with an anatomic focus.
journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery

sections.label: INTRODUCTION
sections.text: Spondylolysis is most commonly observed in the lumbar spine, particularly L5, and is associated with spondylolisthesis, or anterior "slippage" of a vertebra in relation to an adjacent vertebra. Isthmic spondylolisthesis is the result of a pars interarticularis defect and will be the only type of spondylolisthesis addressed in this review.

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Spondylolysis and spondylolisthesis represent a relatively common cause of low back pain, especially in young athletes, and a less common cause of neurologic compromise. When discovered in a symptomatic patient with corroborating imaging findings, early intervention provides an excellent prognosis. Herein, we review the anatomy and pathology of spondylosis and spondylolisthesis of the L5 vertebra.
